Following Trump's return to the White House in January 2025, Washington's interest in Pakistan's crypto and minerals sectors grew, largely driven by close ties between the American president and Pakistan's rulers. However, with a Democrat-led Congress initiating business in January, increased scrutiny on executive dealings could change attitudes toward Pakistan. Indications of this shift include American hesitation regarding Pakistan's request for a $10 billion Exchange Stabilisation Support Facility.

Despite potential challenges, experts suggest that Pakistan-US relations do not inevitably have to decline. Rather than relying solely on personal rapport with the current occupant of the White House, Pakistan should focus on building institutional relationships across all tiers of the US government based on mutual respect and benefit. These ties must remain grounded in mutual interests without compromising Pakistan's other vital partnerships, particularly with China. Over the long term, a balanced approach in South Asia is considered to be in America's own interest for regional stability.

stories.title: Pakistan and Russia Expand Bilateral Technology and IT Cooperation
stories.summary:
Pakistan and Russia have agreed to transition their technology cooperation from dialogue to practical business engagement by pursuing direct company partnerships, joint ventures, and commercial agreements in emerging tech sectors. The commitment was formalized during the Pakistan-Russia IT Collaboration Webinar, which was organized by the Pakistan Software Export Board (PSEB) in collaboration with the University of World Civilizations Moscow (UWCM). The event took place at the Ministry of Planning, Development and Special Initiatives in Islamabad, with Russian participants joining from Moscow.

Discussions during the event focused on six key areas of mutual strength: artificial intelligence and cloud computing, cybersecurity and critical infrastructure protection, digital governance and infrastructure, IT services trade and investment, digital skills exchange, and quantum computing. Federal Minister for Planning, Development and Special Initiatives Ahsan Iqbal served as the chief guest, highlighting that under the national economic transformation plan URAAN Pakistan, technology is a core driver aimed at building a one-trillion-dollar economy by 2035. Iqbal noted Pakistan's growing IT sector, which generated record exports of $4.6 billion in fiscal year 2025-26, alongside initiatives to produce 75,000 IT graduates annually and train one million AI professionals by 2030.

Russian Deputy Minister of Digital Development, Communications and Mass Media Bella Cherkesova delivered the keynote address covering policy and investment in digital partnerships. Meanwhile, Pakistani Ambassador to the Russian Federation Faisal Niaz Tirmizi and PSEB CEO Faisal Jeddy outlined frameworks to connect software industries and transition initial contacts into formal commercial contracts. Additional industry leaders from both nations, including RUSSOFT President Valentin Makarov and P@SHA Chairman Dr Shoab Ahmed Khan, participated in sessions to explore co-development opportunities in cybersecurity, enterprise software, and fintech.

Concluding the webinar, Ministry of IT and Telecommunication Secretary Zarrar Hasham Khan stated that the event yielded concrete collaboration opportunities in AI, cloud computing, and cybersecurity. The ministry's focus will now shift to regulatory facilitation, market intelligence, and reducing operational friction to ensure that pilot projects between Pakistani and Russian firms can commence without delay.

stories.title: PTCL CEO Stresses Reliable Connectivity for Industrial Operational Efficiency
stories.summary:
Pakistan Telecommunication Company Limited (PTCL) Chief Executive Officer Nadeem Khan reaffirmed the company's dedication to providing dependable connectivity, calling it vital for business continuity and operational efficiency. Speaking at the Pakistan Textile Exporters Association (PTEA) on Thursday, Khan detailed PTCL's efforts to modernize service standards and upgrade infrastructure to satisfy the demands of industrial clusters, particularly in Faisalabad, which serves as the heart of Pakistan's textile value chain.

Khan outlined a roadmap to replace legacy copper infrastructure with advanced fibre-optic networks across major industrial areas. This transition is intended to provide export-oriented businesses with the high-speed, low-latency connectivity required for enterprise resource planning systems, international video conferences, and cloud-based supply chain management. He emphasized that digital infrastructure must match the resilience of manufacturing capabilities, noting that PTCL is investing in fibreization, network redundancy, and backup power systems at local exchanges to mitigate the impact of power outages and technical faults.

PTEA Chairman Rehan Naseem Bharara addressed the connectivity challenges faced by member industries, emphasizing the necessity of scalable bandwidth as textile manufacturing increasingly incorporates automated looms, digital printing, and e-commerce fulfilment. Bharara noted that reliable telecommunications are crucial for fulfilling international buyers' requirements and ensuring timely export shipments. He offered PTEA's support in facilitating implementation, proposing a joint working mechanism and technical surveys of identified industrial estates to accelerate fibre deployment and quality enhancements.

stories.title: Indian Stocks Anticipate Pullback Following Strong Rally and Global Selloff
stories.summary:
Indian shares are projected to break their six-session winning streak on Friday following a severe selloff in global markets and investor caution regarding US Democratic policies on AI regulations and foreign policy. Both the Nifty 50 and BSE Sensex achieved their best session in seven months on Thursday, driven by lower oil prices and massive foreign fund inflows. Foreign institutional investors purchased approximately 150 billion rupees ($1.6 billion) in stocks, marking their largest single-day net purchase in nearly six years as global investors rotated away from AI-linked trades.

GIFT Nifty futures stood at 24,460, pointing to a weaker opening for the benchmark Nifty 50, which had closed at 24,536.6 on Thursday. According to Hariselvan Radhakrishnan, founder and CEO of HST Wealth, the expected decline remains relatively contained compared to severe global drops because lower crude prices and limited direct exposure to the AI-hardware trade offer some domestic insulation. Analysts predict a volatile trading session characterized by consolidation and profit-booking.

Investor sentiment turned risk-averse overnight following a sharp decline in US technology stocks, where the Nasdaq dropped 5.5% and the Dow Jones and S&P 500 fell 3.4% and 4.4% respectively, pressured by weak Qualcomm results and slowing AI infrastructure spending. Asian markets followed Wall Street downward on Friday, with South Korea's Kospi dropping 8% and Japan's Nikkei declining 5%.

stories.title: Raja Nasir Abbas Blames Ruling Establishment for Imran Khan Ouster
stories.summary:
Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf-backed opposition leader in the Senate, Raja Nasir Abbas, accused the ruling establishment of orchestrating the removal of Imran Khan under US directions. Speaking to reporters outside Parliament House in Islamabad on Thursday, Abbas stated that this political decision created deep security and political instability across the nation. He criticized the displacement of a democratically elected government in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa that held a two-thirds majority, arguing that governance had been handed over to rejected groups.

Abbas contended that the forces currently tasked with bringing peace to Khyber Pakhtunkhwa had previously helped weaken the system itself. He compared the current domestic situation to flawed international interventions by the US, such as spending over USD 2.2 trillion in Afghanistan without reaching its goals and invading Iraq on false justifications. According to Abbas, prejudices, arrogance, and the misuse of power repeatedly drive leaders into making disastrous choices.

The senator highlighted the ongoing security crises in the country, noting that Balochistan has lacked lasting peace for 25 years while unrest rises in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. He condemned the government for suppressing political dissent, citing the imprisonment of women and alleged abductions of political opponents. Abbas warned that ignoring the electorate's mandate has severely damaged political, social, and economic institutions.

Concluding his remarks, Abbas asserted that the ruling elite treats itself as a privileged class while ignoring public choices. He maintained that the administration is currently fighting the populace instead of serving them. The suppression of opposition and the concentration of power, he added, continue to worsen the country's ongoing economic and domestic security challenges.

stories.title: Dollar Stables and Yen Rises Amid US Equity Selloff
stories.summary:
The US dollar remained stable against major currencies on Friday following a steep selloff in American equities. Driven by a Democratic sweep in Congress and growing concerns over artificial intelligence industry regulations, investors sought shelter in safe-haven assets. This market retreat pushed Treasury yields lower and propelled the Nasdaq to its largest one-day drop since April 2025.

Amid the flight to safety, the Japanese yen strengthened by 0.2 percent to a one-week high of 157.40 per dollar before paring some gains. The Swiss franc also advanced by 0.2 percent against the greenback, while the dollar index held near 101.55. Analysts noted that falling US yields countered the dollar's traditional safe-haven appeal, positioning the yen as a primary hedge against domestic US volatility.

The broader bond market reaction drove the 10-year Treasury yield down to 4.84 percent during Asian morning trading, marking its lowest level since September 10. The two-year yield dropped about 10 basis points to 4.47 percent. Traders adjusted expectations for the Federal Reserve, reducing the probability of a December interest rate hike from over 80 percent to approximately 70 percent ahead of a crucial payrolls report.

Market participants turned their attention to the upcoming US non-farm payrolls data to evaluate the Federal Reserve's future interest rate path. Previous data showed weekly initial jobless claims decreasing by 6,000 to a seasonally adjusted 189,000, mirroring a 57-year low seen in July. Meanwhile, the euro remained flat at $1.222, and the British pound rose 0.1 percent to $1.3457 following a widely expected policy rate increase by the Bank of England.

stories.title: Netanyahu's Coalition Struggles as Arab Parties Back Eisenkot
stories.summary:
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu faced a political setback on Thursday after losing key support from the ultra-Orthodox party United Torah Judaism and seeing two Arab-led parties endorse his main rival, Gadi Eisenkot. President Isaac Herzog continued a second day of political consultations in Jerusalem to determine who will be tasked with forming a government following the inconclusive October 27 election.

Although Netanyahu's Likud Party secured 27 seats to win the most individual mandates, his broader nationalist-religious bloc dropped to 53 seats, falling short of a governing majority in the 120-seat Knesset. Meanwhile, Eisenkot's coalition of centre-left and right-wing Jewish-led parties won 48 seats. Parties representing Israel's Arab minority achieved an unprecedented 19 seats, driven by voter anger against Netanyahu's hard-right administration, and both the Joint List and Raam officially endorsed Eisenkot.

The endorsement from the Arab lists provides Eisenkot with backing from a comfortable majority of lawmakers. However, both Eisenkot and Netanyahu have previously ruled out forming a government with Arab parties, as reliance on them could alienate hardline opposition figures like Avigdor Liberman. Concurrently, United Torah Judaism announced it would not recommend any Knesset member to form a government, prioritizing issues such as the status of Torah students over endorsing either candidate.

President Herzog has until November 11 to choose a nominee, traditionally favoring the candidate recommended by the highest number of parties. Once designated, the chosen lawmaker will have 28 days to build a coalition, with a potential 14-day extension. Netanyahu will continue to serve as prime minister heading a caretaker government until a new coalition is successfully established.

stories.title: Jamaat-i-Islami Reports Petroleum Levy Talks Nearing Final Stage
stories.summary:
Jamaat-i-Islami deputy chief Liaqat Baloch announced on Thursday that negotiations with the government regarding the petroleum levy have entered their final phase. Speaking to journalists in Islamabad after chairing a party meeting, Baloch stated that Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif is ultimately responsible for ensuring the success of the talks. He warned that his party reserves the right to launch a protest march if the administration fails to deliver tangible relief to the public.

Baloch emphasized that Jamaat-i-Islami has made sincere efforts to allow the negotiation process to work toward a peaceful resolution. The party's core objective, he noted, is securing sustainable relief that can stimulate economic activity rather than temporary measures. During his diplomatic efforts, Baloch contacted Deputy Prime Minister Ishaq Dar and Federal Planning Minister Ahsan Iqbal, who chairs the government negotiating committee, to urge timely decisions on the matter.

In response, Deputy Prime Minister Dar stated he was occupied with visiting diplomatic leaders and would communicate the government's subsequent steps by the following day to keep discussions productive. Party experts briefed the Jamaat-i-Islami leadership on the latest progress, confirming that a joint technical committee had been established. Representatives noted that technical experts previously held a meeting at the finance ministry and were awaiting final government directives.

Baloch stated that previous rounds of talks, including a direct meeting between the Prime Minister and the Jamaat-i-Islami chief, established a mutual understanding. Under this understanding, the government is expected to provide consumer relief and progressively eliminate the tax he described as unjust. Further developments on expanding the fuel relief scheme will be evaluated by the joint technical committee.

stories.title: World Bank Report Reveals Pakistan’s External Debt Reached $135.1 Billion
stories.summary:
According to the International Debt Report 2026 released by the World Bank, Pakistan's total external debt climbed from $68.673 billion in 2015 to $135.107 billion by 2025. This substantial increase highlights a decade of continuous borrowing that has brought the country's external liabilities to roughly double their amount from ten years prior.

The overall debt figure for 2025 comprises several components, including $107.076 billion in public and publicly guaranteed debt, $17.58 billion in private non-guaranteed debt, and $10.45 billion in short-term debt. Within the public and publicly guaranteed category, $56.83 billion is owed to multilateral creditors, $42.43 billion to bilateral creditors, and $7.8 billion to private creditors.

China remains the single largest individual creditor for Pakistan, holding $22.4 billion in outstanding loans. Other major lenders include the World Bank with $19.2 billion and the Asian Development Bank at $16.83 billion. To help manage stability, China extended the maturities on $2 billion of loans in 2025, while the International Monetary Fund disbursed $2.3 billion through Extended Fund Facility and Resilience and Sustainability Facility arrangements.

Globally, the World Bank report highlighted that external debt in low- and middle-income countries hit a record $9.4 trillion. While developing economies experienced higher debt-to-income ratios and rising interest burdens, the data underscores the ongoing financial pressures and high borrowing costs facing nations like Pakistan in the global credit market.

stories.title: خیبر پختونخوا میں بچیوں کی شادی کی عمر اٹھارہ سال کرنے کی درخواست
stories.summary:
پشاور ہائیکورٹ میں خیبر پختونخوا کے اندر بچیوں کی شادی کی قانونی عمر سولہ سال مقرر ہونے کے خلاف ایک رٹ پٹیشن دائر کر دی گئی ہے۔ یہ آئینی درخواست لینا قمر اور ماہم نفیس کی جانب سے وکیل عمران خان ایڈووکیٹ کے توسط سے عدالت میں جمع کروائی گئی۔ اس قانونی کارروائی میں وفاقی حکومت، صوبائی حکومت، سیکرٹری قانون اور دیگر متعلقہ اداروں کو فریق بنایا گیا ہے۔

درخواست گزاروں کی طرف سے مؤقف اختیار کیا گیا ہے کہ ملک کے دیگر تمام صوبوں میں لڑکیوں کی شادی کی کم از کم عمر اٹھارہ سال مقرر ہے، مگر خیبر پختونخوا میں یہ حد اب بھی سولہ سال پر برقرار ہے۔ درخواست میں مزید وضاحت کی گئی ہے کہ اٹھارہویں آئینی ترمیم کے بعد اسلام آباد، سندھ، پنجاب اور بلوچستان کی حکومتوں نے شادی سے متعلقہ قوانین میں ترامیم کر لی تھیں، تاہم خیبر پختونخوا میں قانون پرانا ہی چلا آ رہا ہے۔

درخواست میں نشاندہی کی گئی ہے کہ کم عمری میں شادیوں کے انعقاد کی وجہ سے معاشرے میں متعدد خاندانی مسائل جنم لے رہے ہیں۔ اس صورتحال کو سنگین نوعیت کا قرار دیتے ہوئے عدالت سے استدعا کی گئی ہے کہ خیبر پختونخوا میں بھی بچیوں کی شادی کی مجاز عمر کو سولہ سال سے بڑھا کر اٹھارہ سال کیا جائے۔

اس پٹیشن کے دائر ہونے سے صوبے میں کم عمر بچیوں کی شادیوں اور قانونی خامیوں کا معاملہ ایک بار پھر زیرِ بحث آ گیا ہے۔ درخواست گزاروں کا مقصد صوبائی قانون کو ملک کے باقی حصوں اور اٹھارہویں ترمیم کے تقاضوں کے مطابق ہم آہنگ کرنا ہے تاکہ خاندانی تنازعات پر قابو پایا جا سکے اور بچیوں کے حقوق کا تحفظ ممکن بنایا جا سکے۔

stories.title: World Bank Report Shows Pakistan’s External Debt Rose to $135.1 Billion
stories.summary:
Pakistan's total external debt experienced a dramatic upward trajectory, nearly doubling over the decade leading up to 2025 to reach $135.107 billion, up from $68.673 billion in 2015. The findings come directly from the International Debt Report 2026 published by the World Bank.

A breakdown of the 2025 figures shows that the nation's liabilities include $107.076 billion in public and publicly guaranteed debt, $17.58 billion in private non-guaranteed debt, and $10.45 billion in short-term obligations. Publicly backed debt consists of $56.83 billion owed to multilateral institutions, $42.43 billion to bilateral partners, and $7.8 billion to private entities.

Among individual creditors, China stands as Pakistan's largest lender with $22.4 billion outstanding. The World Bank follows with $19.2 billion, and the Asian Development Bank holds $16.83 billion. During 2025, economic support measures included China extending maturities on $2 billion in loans and the International Monetary Fund issuing $2.3 billion in new disbursements via the Extended Fund Facility and Resilience and Sustainability Facility.

The broader regional context noted that the Middle East, North Africa, Afghanistan, and Pakistan region saw its external debt-to-gross national income ratio increase to 29.4 percent in 2025. This metric reflects the steepest single-year regional rise, demonstrating persistent debt accumulation amidst shifting global economic conditions.

stories.title: UK Court Increases Killer's Sentence in Racially Motivated Murder Case
stories.summary:
England’s Court of Appeal has extended the prison sentence of Vickrum Digwa, a British Sikh convicted of murdering 18-year-old student Henry Nowak last year. A three-judge panel ruled that the original minimum life term of 21 years was unduly lenient, increasing it to 25 years minus the 175 days he already spent on remand.

Chief Judge Sue Carr delivered the ruling on Thursday, stating that the initial punishment failed to appropriately reflect the severe nature of the crime. During the December attack in Southampton, Digwa repeatedly stabbed Nowak and falsely told police officers that the teenager had racially abused him while Nowak lay dying in handcuffs.

The racially tinged homicide generated widespread public outrage and triggered violent protests across Britain. High-profile figures, including Reform UK leader Nigel Farage and US tech billionaire Elon Musk, capitalized on the incident to highlight alleged discrimination against white Britons.

In addition to Digwa's sentencing, his mother, Kiran Kaur, received a three-year prison term for attempting to conceal the ceremonial knife used in the attack. While Nowak's family welcomed the increased sentence, they emphasized that their suffering persists and pledged to support an independent government review into the circumstances of the killing announced the previous week.

stories.title: Pakistan Reaches Record Foreign Exchange Reserves Despite Gulf War Pressures
stories.summary:
Pakistan's foreign exchange reserves have surged to an all-time high exceeding $26.8 billion, according to data released by the State Bank of Pakistan (SBP) on Thursday. This milestone was achieved despite economic turbulence and high oil prices stemming from the Gulf war, which commenced on February 28 and disrupted weaker economies globally.

The central bank has successfully expanded its reserves by more than $5 billion since February, when holdings stood at $16.568 billion, reaching $21.568 billion by October 30. During the latest reported week, SBP reserves grew by $39 million, while commercial bank reserves climbed by $70 million, pushing total country reserves to $26.864 billion compared to $26.754 billion the previous week.

Financial analysts consider the current volume of reserves sufficient to maintain exchange rate stability and encourage exporters to promptly return earnings. However, currency experts argue that the rupee remains overvalued, which has lowered dollar costs for importers and caused the trade deficit for July through October of fiscal year 2027 to widen to $14.6 billion, driven by $26 billion in imports against $11.4 billion in exports.

Critics also point out that the stable exchange rate is maintained partly through steady worker remittances, which are traditionally utilized to bridge the trade gap rather than supporting a dedicated government deployment policy.

stories.title: Pakistan wastes Rs3.5 trillion annually on energy sector mismanagement and imports
stories.summary:
Pakistan suffers an annual loss of Rs3.5 trillion due to unnecessary and rising energy-sector imports caused by administrative mismanagement, delayed building codes, and a failure to implement local manufacturing plans. This issue was highlighted at an Islamabad event on Pakistan's Energy Security organized by the LUMS Energy Institute, featuring speakers like National Grid Pakistan Chairman Dr Fiaz Chaudhry, Independent System and Market Operator CEO Dr Masood Ahmad, and NGP CEO Altaf Hussain Malik.

Experts pointed out that although Pakistan's electricity generation capacity exceeds 36,000MW, the base load of about 8,000MW remained stagnant between 2015 and 2023, particularly during the four winter months. Consequently, the nation spends $2.7 billion importing liquefied natural gas for winter heating while massive generation capacity sits idle, driving up capacity payments and circular debt. Although the federal government approved an energy conservation building code in 2023 that could reduce cooling loads by 51 percent, provinces like Punjab, Sindh, and Balochistan have yet to adopt it, whereas the Capital Development Authority and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa have begun implementation.

Research indicates that improving energy efficiency in just 25 percent of residential homes could slash peak electricity demand by approximately 3,000MW and save Rs442.6 billion annually. Furthermore, a proposed Net Zero Transition model aims to cut fossil-fuel generation from 49 percent in fiscal year 2024 to about 1 percent by fiscal year 2040. Experts also identified Rs1.1 trillion in potential domestic equipment manufacturing opportunities to replace current imports.

Speakers urged authorities to expedite the long-delayed Power Sector Indigenisation Plan to revive local industries that previously produced necessary spares and equipment prior to the 1998 Wapda unbundling. Implementing integrated system planning and local manufacturing is vital for enhancing long-term energy security and economic stability.

stories.title: Pakistan's first Marble City industrial park is being established in Karachi
stories.summary:
Sindh Minister for Information, Transport and Mass Transit Sharjeel Inam Memon announced the establishment of Pakistan's first Marble City in Karachi to foster investment, boost industrial activity, and create jobs. Speaking at a pre-launch event for the industrial park at a local hotel, he stated that the project will utilize modern techniques to process local marble and granite reserves into high-quality finished products for international export, rather than selling them as raw materials.

The formal inauguration will be conducted jointly by Pakistan Peoples Party Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari and Sindh Chief Minister Murad Ali Shah. Land within the Marble City is priced at roughly Rs25 million per acre, with flexible installment options provided for investors unable to make upfront lump-sum payments. Special Assistant to the Chief Minister on Investment Qasim Naveed Qamar added that the project spans over 300 acres along the Northern Bypass with an estimated cost of $250 million, developed via a public-private partnership framework.

Mr Qamar noted that the Sindh government is actively working to supply electricity at Rs20 per unit for regional projects like Dhabeji and Khairpur, while aiming to offer subsidized rates and machinery rentals to industrialists within the Marble City. Investor and industrialist registration processes are scheduled to begin next month to extend these operational facilities.

Minister Memon emphasized the broader importance of aligning local resource processing with modern industrial needs to support the national economy. He also welcomed inter-provincial cooperation, stating that Sindh is happy to adopt effective administrative projects from other provinces such as Punjab to encourage positive national development.

stories.title: Developing Nations External Debt Surges to Record $9.4 Trillion
stories.summary:
Low- and middle-income countries experienced a 5.5 percent increase in external debt, pushing the total to a record USD 9.4 trillion in 2025. This marks the largest annual surge since 2021, according to the annual International Debt Report released on Thursday by the Washington-based World Bank. The rising obligations threaten to crowd out essential investments in education, health, jobs, and infrastructure across developing regions.

The poorest nations faced steep borrowing costs, paying an average of 8.2 percent on new private-creditor commitments and 9.4 percent on new bonds, rates not seen since 1989. In contrast, countries ineligible for International Development Association low-interest loans paid an average of 5.5 percent. Overall, developing countries' borrowing from private creditors and public bond issuances jumped nearly 35 percent to USD 251 billion. External debt grew fastest among IDA-eligible nations, climbing 8.1 percent to USD 1.3 trillion.

Governments across the developing world paid a combined USD 1.4 trillion in principal and interest during 2025, marking the fifth consecutive annual increase. Payments to private creditors surged by 13.7 percent to USD 363 billion. Furthermore, a dramatic depreciation of the US dollar drove up the dollar-denominated value of foreign debt, accounting for over 28 percent of the overall increase in debt stock.

World Bank chief statistician Haishan Fu noted that while the return of private lending is welcome, heavy borrowing leaves fewer resources for long-term development. The international lender emphasized the need for responsible debt management, increased transparency, and stronger data standards to help developing nations avoid severe economic vulnerabilities and protect future generations from external shocks.

stories.title: Pakistan External Debt Nears $135 Billion Over Ten Years
stories.summary:
Pakistan’s external debt stock grew by 4 percent to reach USD 135.1 billion in 2025, nearly doubling from USD 68.7 billion in 2015. The World Bank’s International Debt Report 2026 revealed that multilateral and bilateral creditors account for the vast majority of the country's public external obligations, while private borrowing remained significantly more expensive than official financing options.

The nation's end-2025 external debt comprised USD 107.076 billion in public and publicly guaranteed debt, USD 17.58 billion in private non-guaranteed debt, and USD 10.451 billion in short-term obligations. Multilateral institutions held USD 56.832 billion, while bilateral creditors accounted for USD 42.439 billion. China remained the largest bilateral lender with USD 22.419 billion, followed by the World Bank at USD 19.214 billion and the Asian Development Bank at USD 16.830 billion. Additionally, the International Monetary Fund disbursed USD 2.3 billion in 2025 under the Extended Fund Facility and Resilience and Sustainability Facility.

The data illustrated a sharp contrast in borrowing costs. Official creditors offered new commitments averaging a 3.6 percent interest rate with a 16-year maturity and a four-year grace period. Conversely, private creditors charged an average interest rate of 8.6 percent with a short three-year maturity and a one-year grace period, carrying considerably higher financial risks.

Prakistan's external debt-to-gross national income ratio stood at 34 percent, with debt service payments consuming 33 percent of exports and 3 percent of GNI. The country's external debt-to-exports ratio reached 324 percent. The World Bank underscored the importance of improving borrowing terms and expanding export earnings to alleviate refinancing pressures.

stories.title: Prime Minister Sharif Threatens Petrol Pumps Failing Fuel Relief
stories.summary:
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif warned petrol pump operators of strict punitive measures, directing authorities to cancel the licences of any outlets that fail to properly facilitate registered beneficiaries under the national Fuel Relief Programme. The directive was issued during a Thursday meeting in Islamabad focused on reviewing the implementation, transparency, and subsidy disbursements of the welfare scheme.

Officials reported that over 15.5 million citizens had successfully registered for the programme as of November 4, with total subsidy disbursements reaching Rs28.6 billion. The registered beneficiaries include roughly 15.06 million motorcycle owners and 449,000 owners of vehicles with engine capacities up to 800cc. Out of 63,153,685 generated fuel subsidy tokens, 59,445,347 have been successfully redeemed by citizens.

Sharif expressed satisfaction with the high level of transparency and enrolment, attributing the success to simplified registration and subsidy redemption procedures. He praised the technology-based mechanism as a potential game-changer for public welfare and commended Federal Minister for Information Technology Shaza Fatima, Federal Secretary Zarar Hashim Khan, and their teams for establishing a monitoring dashboard and separate call centres for consumer and operator complaints.

The high-level review meeting was attended by Deputy Prime Minister Ishaq Dar, Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb, Information Minister Attaullah Tarar, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik, and several other senior federal ministers and government officials. Sharif stressed that effective monitoring remains vital to ensuring that eligible citizens receive their subsidies without facing unnecessary operational hurdles.

stories.title: WTA Takes Blame After Livestream Captures Pegula Criticizing Andreeva
stories.summary:
The Women’s Tennis Association announced on Thursday that it accepts full responsibility for failing to inform players that microphones were active during practice sessions at Indian Wells, California. The oversight resulted in the broadcast of private remarks made by American tennis player Jessica Pegula regarding Russian competitor Mirra Andreeva on the organization's YouTube livestream ahead of the WTA Finals.

During Thursday's practice session, microphones captured a conversation between world number five Pegula and her coach, Mark Knowles. In the recorded dialogue, Pegula described the 19-year-old French Open champion Andreeva as "a diva" who "needs to be humbled" and suggested that coach Conchita Martinez encouraged the behavior. Clips of the exchange quickly circulated across social media platforms before the WTA removed the session recordings from YouTube.

A representative for Pegula stated that the American player had no idea her practice conversation was being livestreamed and never intended for a private discussion to become public. Pegula, who also serves on the WTA Players' Council, contacted the individuals involved to apologize and had earlier praised Andreeva during the same conversation as wonderful and smart.

The WTA Finals are scheduled to run through November 15, marking the first time the season-ending tournament is being hosted at the Indian Wells Tennis Garden. The governing body's failure to notify athletes of the active audio equipment has sparked significant attention ahead of the tournament's official start on Sunday.

stories.title: ATC Defers Indictment of Accused in Judicial Complex Attack Case
stories.summary:
An Anti-Terrorism Court in Islamabad on Thursday postponed the framing of charges against accused individuals in two cases linked to an alleged attack on the Federal Judicial Complex. Presiding judge Tahir Abbas Sipra delayed the proceedings because of the absence of incarcerated Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf founding chairman and former Prime Minister Imran Khan.

The cases involve two separate first information reports registered by the city police at the Counter Terrorism Department and the Golra Police Station. Authorities accused PTI leaders and workers of attacking police officers and causing unrest outside the judicial complex during a hearing regarding the Toshakhana case against Imran Khan.

The charges against the former prime minister and other leaders include Section 7 of the Anti-Terrorism Act alongside several provisions of the Pakistan Penal Code. These encompass rioting with deadly weapons, obstructing and assaulting public servants on duty, theft, dacoity, mischief causing property damage by fire or explosive substances, and criminal intimidation.

Following the delay, the court rescheduled the hearing for January 2 without taking further action. The matter remains pending due to the continued non-availability of the primary defendant.

This delay highlights ongoing judicial bottlenecks in high-profile political cases involving the opposition party leadership. The outcome of the upcoming January hearing will determine whether the court can formally proceed with the indictments.

stories.title: HESCO Chief Directs One-Month Resolution for Hyderabad Power Supply Issues
stories.summary:
The Hyderabad Chamber of Small Traders & Small Industry recently raised serious concerns regarding power supply difficulties affecting local businesses. President Nadeem Ahmed Siddiqui met with HESCO Chief Faizullah Dahri to discuss the negative impacts of unscheduled load shedding, prolonged shutdowns, and delayed power restoration on industrial feeders.

According to the business delegation, the situation on the SITE, Indus, Hosri, and Fazal Gulzar feeders is particularly alarming. Siddiqui noted that uninterrupted electricity is vital for industrial production and commercial activities, warning that current outages cause significant financial losses and disrupt important evening business hours.

Several other trade representatives attended the meeting to voice their grievances. They stressed the urgent need to improve feeder performance, reduce outage durations, and prioritize electricity delivery to commercial and industrial zones throughout Hyderabad.

In response to the complaints, HESCO Chief Faizullah Dahri directed relevant officials to resolve all electricity supply problems on the affected feeders within a one-month timeframe. He assured the delegation that effective measures would be taken, emphasizing that industries are valued customers deserving of top-priority service.

A follow-up meeting is scheduled for December 4 to review progress made during the month. If issues persist, authorities will take further decisions based on the situation, while the Chamber expressed hope for practical steps to alleviate community difficulties.

stories.title: FBR Revises Property Valuation Framework for Islamabad Rural Areas and Abbottabad
stories.summary:
The Federal Board of Revenue has issued revised valuation mechanisms for immovable properties in rural areas of the Islamabad Capital Territory and Abbottabad. The updated framework took effect on November 5, 2026, under Section 68(4) of the Income Tax Ordinance, 2001, superseding previous notifications from 2024 and earlier in 2026.

Through SRO 2060(I)/2026, the FBR established fresh fair market values for residential and commercial open plots across Abbottabad. Residential plots in locations like Main Bazar and Kutcheri Road are valued at 1.25 million rupees per marla, while Abbottabad Bazar is set at 970,000 rupees. Commercial open plots range from 5.8 million rupees per marla in Main Bazar to 2.5 million rupees in areas such as College Road Mandian and Murree Road.

The Abbottabad notification also introduces depreciation-based valuation rates for constructed buildings. Properties up to five years old are assessed at 2,000 rupees per square foot, buildings between five and ten years at 1,000 rupees, and those older than ten years at 500 rupees, to be added to underlying land valuations.

Separately, SRO 2061(I)/2026 amends earlier rules for Islamabad's rural areas. Property valuations there will now align directly with the latest rates issued periodically by the Additional Deputy Commissioner Revenue and District Collector of Islamabad.

These revisions aim to update tax collection baselines for immovable property transactions in both regions. Tax authorities expect the updated framework to provide clearer guidelines for fair market assessments.

stories.title: Federal Minister Ahsan Iqbal Proposes Autonomous Pakistan Tourism Authority
stories.summary:
Federal Minister for Planning, Development and Special Initiatives Ahsan Iqbal has called for the creation of an autonomous Pakistan Tourism Authority. During a Thursday meeting with Information and Broadcasting Minister Attaullah Tarar, Iqbal stated that the proposed body should include representation from all four provinces to improve national coordination and internationally market Pakistan as a unified tourism destination.

The discussion took place as Prime Minister’s Adviser on Tourism, Sardar Ayaz, briefed officials on tourism promotion initiatives and achievements spanning 2025–26. Participants emphasized the necessity of strong institutional mechanisms and policy frameworks to harness the country's natural beauty and tourism potential effectively.

During the briefing, Sardar Ayaz announced that the Pakistan Tourism, Sports and Family Festival 2026 is scheduled for November 6, 7, and 8 in Islamabad. Various recreational events will take place across the capital, including at Lake View Park, with financial support secured through private sector sponsorships.

Iqbal stressed that a cohesive national strategy is vital for positioning Pakistan prominently on the global tourism map. Enhanced cooperation between federal and provincial authorities forms the cornerstone of this proposed developmental approach.

The meeting concluded with a shared focus on advancing institutional cooperation to boost both tourism and sports sectors. Officials hope these coordinated efforts will drive economic growth and attract higher numbers of international visitors.

stories.title: Business Groups Form Alliance Ahead of FPCCI Elections
stories.summary:
The Businessmen Group (BMG) and Businessmen Panel (BMP) have united to form the Pakistan Businessmen Alliance (PBA) to jointly contest the upcoming Federation of Pakistan Chambers of Commerce and Industry (FPCCI) elections. Announced at a Karachi press conference on Thursday by BMG Chairman Zubair Motiwala and BMP Chairman Mian Anjum Nisar, the newly formed alliance aims to challenge the presidential nomination of S.M. Tanveer, the candidate put forward by the United Businessman Group (UBG).

The PBA leaders called for the FPCCI elections to be conducted under the supervision of a retired judge and demanded representation on the election committee to guarantee fairness and transparency. They announced that Zubair Motiwala will run for the position of FPCCI president, with the alliance contesting all available posts. According to Motiwala and Nisar, the coalition was created after the FPCCI Secretary General rejected the nomination papers of the Karachi Chamber and other candidates, sparking worries about fair representation, particularly for the province of Sindh.

Beyond the immediate 2027-28 electoral cycle, the BMG and BMP intend to maintain a long-term partnership to tackle national economic challenges, advocate for reforms, encourage industrialisation, boost exports, attract investments, and generate employment. Motiwala raised concerns regarding the rotational turn allocated to Sindh, questioning the eligibility and electoral records of the rival candidate from Punjab. He emphasized the economic weight of Karachi, which accounts for over 67 percent of national revenue and 54 percent of exports, stating that Sindh's rightful representation must be defended through verifiable documentation and legal channels if necessary.

This political realignment matters because it consolidates major business factions to challenge existing leadership structures within Pakistan's apex trade body. The conflict over provincial rotation and candidate eligibility highlights deep-seated tensions regarding regional representation and institutional fairness in national economic governance.

stories.title: ADB Urges Structural Reforms to Overcome Economic Cycles
stories.summary:
Pakistan must prioritize consistent structural reforms, export diversification, and private-sector-led investments to overcome its recurring boom-and-bust economic cycles. Speaking at the Sustainable Development Policy Institute’s 29th Sustainable Development Conference on Thursday, Asian Development Bank (ADB) Country Director Dr Emma Xiaoqin Fan warned that decades of economic crises have failed to improve per capita income and living standards without institutional stability and policy continuity.

Fan noted that while Pakistan possesses significant potential due to its young population and agricultural resources, macroeconomic stability must be paired with a business-friendly regulatory environment and civil service reforms. She stressed that the government should focus on acting as a facilitator rather than engaging directly in commercial activities, citing the privatisation of Pakistan International Airlines (PIA) as a positive step. Meanwhile, Sam Waldock, Development Director at the British High Commission, highlighted that Pakistan's growth ceiling hovers around 3.8 percent because imports outpace exports, creating balance-of-payments pressures. Waldock outlined key export priorities, including regulatory reforms, trade facilitation, and market-oriented skills development to address weaknesses in export competitiveness.

Pernille Ironside, Acting UN Resident Coordinator and UNICEF Country Representative, added that the success of economic reforms must be measured by their tangible impact on human development, such as improved education, healthcare, and employment opportunities for the youth. The discussions emphasized that predictable policymaking, reduced compliance costs for businesses, and targeted public spending are vital for long-term national progress.

Addressing these structural bottlenecks is critical for Pakistan to escape chronic financial instability and unlock sustainable economic growth. The insights provided by international development partners underscore the urgent need for policy consistency and institutional reform to support a population of over 250 million people.

stories.title: Prime Minister Calls for Action Plan After New Polio Case
stories.summary:
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif directed federal health authorities on Thursday to draft a coordinated national action plan within a week following the confirmation of Pakistan's ninth polio case of the year. The latest infection was detected in the Khyber district, bringing the total number of cases for the week to nine during a high-level review meeting in Islamabad.

Officials reported that seven of the nine cases originated in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, specifically across Khyber, Bannu, and North Waziristan districts, while the remaining two cases were found in Karachi East and Sujawal in Sindh. Health authorities informed the meeting that the three cases in Khyber were linked to poliovirus strains circulating in Afghanistan, underscoring cross-border movement as a primary vector for transmission. In response, Sharif instructed the federal health minister, health secretary, and eradication team members to immediately consult provincial chief ministers and chief secretaries to build an integrated response.

The prime minister emphasized the importance of enhancing routine immunisation coverage in high-risk areas while ensuring the safety of frontline vaccination workers operating in security-sensitive regions. Officials noted that while access for immunization teams has improved in several challenging locations, Punjab, Balochistan, Azad Jammu and Kashmir, and Gilgit-Baltistan have reported stable or polio-free statuses over recent periods.

This renewed push matters as authorities attempt to curb the resurgence of the poliovirus and address cross-border transmission channels. Effective federal-provincial coordination and worker safety remain central to achieving a polio-free Pakistan.

stories.title: Groundbreaking Held for New State Lounge at Islamabad Airport
stories.summary:
Pakistan has officially commenced the construction of a new State Lounge at Islamabad International Airport to host visiting heads of state and foreign dignitaries. Federal Minister for Defence Khawaja Muhammad Asif laid the foundation stone for the project during a groundbreaking ceremony held on Thursday.

The infrastructure upgrade is part of the government's ongoing preparations to host the upcoming Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Council of Heads of State Summit, scheduled for August 2027. The new facility is designed to elevate state protocol, hospitality, and facilitation standards for international delegations, senior government officials, and foreign leaders. Attendees at the ceremony included Secretary Defence Lt Gen Muhammad Ali (retd), Pakistan Airports Authority (PAA) Director General AVM Muhammad Shahid Afzaal, and other senior defense and aviation officials.

Following the groundbreaking, the defence minister unveiled a commemorative plaque and participated in a tree planting activity to highlight the government's focus on environmental sustainability. According to the PAA, the state lounge project is a key component of wider national infrastructure improvements aimed at supporting high-level diplomatic events.

Initiating this project is crucial for ensuring that Pakistan's aviation and protocol facilities meet international standards ahead of the high-profile SCO summit in 2027. The development reflects broader efforts to strengthen national hospitality and logistical frameworks for major international engagements.

stories.title: Punjab Chief Minister Orders Strict Crop Residue Ban and District Review
stories.summary:
Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz Sharif has instructed deputy commissioners to completely halt the burning of crop residue while warning officials in Okara and other districts for inadequate performance. During a meeting evaluating administrative progress, she reviewed key performance indicators presented by Punjab Performance Management Unit head and Special Assistant Shoaib Mirza. The chief minister commended several district administrations, including Murree, Gujranwala, Attock, Bahawalpur, Chakwal, Jhelum, Layyah, and Sahiwal, while expressing dissatisfaction with delays and substandard execution in various beautification initiatives.

To improve urban management and public safety, the administration was ordered to ensure operational streetlights, covered manholes, and enhanced zebra crossings alongside school safety measures. Deputy commissioners and assistant commissioners were directed to conduct daily hospital visits, deep cleaning, and road washings, while also repairing water filtration plants and bus terminals. Officials established a strict three-step policy against vacant plots used for garbage dumping, moving from warnings to heavy fines and eventual FIR registrations. Additionally, province-wide crackdowns were ordered against encroachments, wall chalking, stray dogs, and unauthorized advertising banners.

The discussions also encompassed district economic planning, university outreach programs, and specific beautification projects across regions like Khanewal, Mian Channu, Jahanian, Sheikhupura, Sharaqpur, Muridke, Eminabad, Kamoke, and Nowshera Virkan. In Rahim Yar Khan, the chief minister directed that food streets and carts be transferred to capable individuals due to plan deviations. Authorities reviewed metrics covering eBiz platforms, dog-bite cases, price controls, and citizen services, with the chief minister warning that administrative negligence directly impacts her reputation.

stories.title: پاکستان اور تاجکستان کی دوطرفہ مشترکہ فوجی مشق دوستی تھری اختتام پذیر
stories.summary:
پاکستان اور تاجکستان کے درمیان دوطرفہ انسداد دہشت گردی کی مشترکہ مشق 'دوستی III' اختتام پذیر ہو گئی ہے۔ آئی ایس پی آر کے مطابق یہ دو ہفتے جاری رہنے والی مشق اسپیشل آپریشنز اسکول چیراٹ میں منعقد کی گئی جس کا آغاز چھبیس اکتوبر کو ہوا تھا۔

اس مشق کا بنیادی مقصد دونوں ممالک کی افواج کے درمیان انسداد دہشت گردی کے تجربات کا تبادلہ کرنا، آپریشنل مشقوں کو بہتر بنانا اور جنگی مہارتوں کو نکھارنا تھا۔ مشق کے دوران دونوں ممالک کے فوجیوں نے انسداد دہشت گردی کے طریقہ کار اور بہترین طریقوں سے استفادہ کیا۔

یہ فوجی مشق پاکستان اور تاجکستان کے مابین دیرینہ اور مضبوط دفاعی تعاون کی مظہر ہے۔ اس طرح کے اقدامات دونوں دوست ممالک کے درمیان دفاعی تعلقات کو مزید مستحکم کرنے اور علاقائی سطح پر سکیورٹی کے امور میں تعاون بڑھانے کے عزم کی عکاسی کرتے ہیں۔

stories.title: Trump Warns Iran of Potential Destruction While IRGC Claims Drones Downed
stories.summary:
US President Donald Trump stated on Thursday that he may need to "destroy the rest" of Iran and remarked that the public would know his next steps soon. Speaking in the Oval Office, Trump noted that he would prefer to avoid further destruction of the country but mentioned that rebuilding from the ongoing conflict could take twenty-five years. When questioned about proposals regarding Iran's nuclear program delivered through mediators, Trump asserted that Tehran does not take actions without American approval.

The remarks coincide with ongoing military tensions stemming from the US-Israeli offensive against Iran that commenced on February 28. On the same day, Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) announced that its Aerospace Force utilized advanced electronic warfare systems to bring down two US MQM-170 reconnaissance drones over Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz.

The IRGC stated that these incidents bring the total number of downed MQM-170 drones to six during the ongoing conflict, though no further details were provided regarding the latest operation. Tehran and Washington continue to experience heightened military friction as diplomatic efforts and regional developments unfold.

stories.title: بہترین کارکردگی کے باوجود قومی بیٹر شان مسعود مستقبل کے پلانز سے باہر
stories.summary:
پاکستان کے لیے گزشتہ دو برس کے دوران سب سے زیادہ رنز بنانے والے ٹاپ بیٹر شان مسعود ٹیم کے مستقبل کے پلانز سے باہر ہو گئے ہیں۔ انہیں بنگلادیش کے خلاف دو ٹیسٹ میچوں کی سیریز کے لیے قومی اسکواڈ میں شامل نہیں کیا گیا حالانکہ وہ مکمل طور پر فٹ بھی نہیں تھے۔

ٹیسٹ کوچ مائیک ہیسن نے نوجوان کھلاڑیوں پر انحصار کرنے کا فیصلہ کیا ہے جس کے تحت شان مسعود کو آگاہ کر دیا گیا ہے کہ وہ آئندہ کی حکمت عملی کا حصہ نہیں ہیں۔ شان نے جنوری 2025 سے اب تک مجموعی طور پر 773 رنز بنائے جبکہ بابر اعظم 720 رنز کے ساتھ دوسرے اور محمد رضوان 643 رنز کے ساتھ تیسرے بہترین بیٹر رہے۔

اگرچہ شان مسعود نے انگلینڈ کے خلاف آخری ٹیسٹ میں 95 رنز کی شاندار اننگز کھیلی تھی اور گزشتہ سال بھی ان کی اوسط بہتر رہی تھی، تاہم بورڈ حکام اور سلیکٹرز کی گڈ بکس سے نکل جانے کی وجہ سے انہیں نظر انداز کیا گیا۔ دوسری طرف سینئر کھلاڑی محمد عباس کو منتخب کر کے عمر کی پالیسی کو بھی نظر انداز کیا گیا ہے۔

stories.title: پاکستان اور ترکیہ کے درمیان لائیو اسٹاک اور ویکسین کی تیاری میں تعاون کا فیصلہ
stories.summary:
پاکستان اور ترکیہ کے مابین لائیو اسٹاک کے شعبے میں تعاون کو فروغ دینے کے لیے ایک اہم پیشرفت سامنے آئی ہے۔ وفاقی وزیر برائے قومی غذائی تحفظ و تحقیق رانا تنویر حسین اور ترکیہ کے سفیر ڈاکٹر عرفان نذیر اوغلو کے درمیان اسلام آباد میں ایک ملاقات ہوئی جس میں لائیو اسٹاک کی ترقی، ویکسین کی مقامی تیاری اور تکنیکی تربیت جیسے امور پر تفصیلی تبادلہ خیال کیا گیا۔

اس مجوزہ پروگرام کے تحت مجموعی طور پر ایک سو پاکستانی افراد کو تربیت فراہم کی جائے گی، جس کے پہلے مرحلے میں تیس افراد کو خصوصی تربیت حاصل کرنے کے لیے ترکیہ روانہ کیا جائے گا۔ ترکیہ کی تکنیکی معاونت کی بدولت پاکستان میں منہ کھر کی بیماری سے بچاؤ کے لیے مقامی سطح پر ویکسین تیار کی جائے گی۔

ویکسین کی مقامی سطح پر تیاری اور جانوروں کی صحت کے لیے کیے جانے والے بہتر اقدامات سے ملک میں بیماری سے پاک زونز کے قیام میں مدد ملے گی۔ اس کے علاوہ ان تمام اقدامات کا بنیادی مقصد ملک سے گوشت کی برآمدات میں خاطر خواہ اضافہ کرنا ہے۔

stories.title: ترک پارلیمنٹ نے پاکستان اور سعودی عرب کے ساتھ دفاعی معاہدے کی توثیق کردی
stories.summary:
ترکیہ کی پارلیمنٹ نے پاکستان، سعودی عرب اور ترکیہ کے درمیان طے پانے والے مکہ مشترکہ دفاعی معاہدے کی باضابطہ توثیق کر دی ہے۔ ترک میڈیا کے مطابق اس معاہدے کے حق میں دو سو اناسی ووٹ ڈالے گئے جبکہ ایک سو انیس ارکان نے اس کی مخالفت کی، اور چھ سو ارکان پر مشتمل ترک پارلیمنٹ میں کل تین سو اٹھانویں ارکان نے اس ووٹنگ کے عمل میں حصہ لیا۔

ترک پارلیمنٹ کی خارجہ امور کمیٹی کے چیئرمین کا اس حوالے سے کہنا ہے کہ یہ اتحاد مکمل طور پر دفاعی نوعیت کا حامل ہے اور اس کا مقصد کسی بھی دوسرے ملک کے خلاف کوئی جارحانہ کارروائی کرنا نہیں ہے۔ حکمراں جماعت جسٹس اینڈ ڈیولپمنٹ پارٹی کے رکن ضیا آلتونیالدز نے بھی اس بات کی تائید کرتے ہوئے کہا کہ اس معاہدے کا اصل مقصد خطے کے اندر سکیورٹی کے شعبے میں تعاون کو مزید فروغ دینا ہے۔

واضح رہے کہ پاکستان، سعودی عرب اور ترکیہ نے سات اگست کو مکہ مکرمہ میں اس مشترکہ دفاعی معاہدے پر دستخط کیے تھے، جس کی تقریب میں وزیراعظم شہباز شریف، سعودی ولی عہد محمد بن سلمان اور ترک صدر رجب طیب اردوان شریک ہوئے تھے۔ پارلیمنٹ کی جانب سے توثیق کے بعد اب اس معاہدے پر عملی نفاذ کے لیے تمام متعلقہ قانونی اور انتظامی مراحل انتہائی اہمیت کے حامل ہوں گے۔

stories.title: امریکی وزیر دفاع پیٹ ہیگسیتھ کا عہدہ چھوڑنے سے انکار اور مواخذے کا سامنا
stories.summary:
امریکی وزیر دفاع پیٹ ہیگسیتھ نے کانگریس کی جانب سے اپنے خلاف لائے جانے والے مواخذے کی کوششوں کا بھرپور مقابلہ کرنے کا تہیہ کر لیا ہے اور انہوں نے ایران کے خلاف کی جانے والی جنگ کا بھی دفاع کیا ہے۔ ان کا موقف ہے کہ یہ فوجی کارروائی ایک جرات مندانہ اور انتہائی تاریخی قدم تھا، اگرچہ رواں ہفتے ہونے والے وسط مدتی انتخابات میں اس جنگ کی وجہ سے ری پبلکنز کو سیاسی نقصان اٹھانا پڑا ہے۔

خبر رساں ادارے رائٹرز کے مطابق پیٹ ہیگسیتھ نے سوشل میڈیا پر جاری کردہ ایک ویڈیو پیغام میں اس عزم کا اظہار کیا ہے کہ وہ پینٹاگون میں رہتے ہوئے اپنے خلاف اٹھنے والی تمام تر کوششوں کا ڈٹ کر سامنا کریں گے۔ ان کا یہ بیان ایسے وقت میں سامنے آیا ہے جب کانگریس کے اندر ان کے سیاسی مخالفین کی تنقید اور مواخذے کے مطالبات میں تیزی سے شدت آ رہی ہے۔ دوسری جانب امریکی صدر ڈونلڈ ٹرمپ نے اپنے وزیر دفاع کو ہٹانے سے متعلق اٹھنے والے سوالات کو یکسر مسترد کرتے ہوئے ان کی بھرپور حمایت کی ہے۔

ایوانِ نمائندگان میں ڈیموکریٹس کے سربراہ حکیم جیفریز نے اس پر سوال اٹھایا ہے کہ پیٹ ہیگسیتھ اب تک اپنے عہدے پر کیوں برقرار ہیں۔ سابق فاکس نیوز میزبان پیٹ ہیگسیتھ کو امریکی سیاست میں ایک متنازع شخصیت سمجھا جاتا ہے جنہیں اپنی ہی ری پبلکن پارٹی کے بعض ارکان کی مخالفت کا بھی سامنا ہے۔ ناقدین کی جانب سے ان پر ایران جنگ سے نمٹنے کے طریقوں، اعلیٰ فوجی افسران کو ہٹانے اور قانون سازوں کے ساتھ کشیدہ تعلقات جیسے معاملات پر شدید نوعیت کے سوالات اٹھائے جا رہے ہیں۔

stories.title: اقوام متحدہ کی رپورٹ کے مطابق افغانستان میں تعلیمی بحران سنگین صورتحال اختیار کر گیا
stories.summary:
افغانستان میں تعلیمی نظام شدید بحران کا شکار ہو چکا ہے جہاں کل ایک کروڑ پندرہ لاکھ بچوں میں سے ستر لاکھ بچے، جو کہ مجموعی طور پر ترپن فیصد بنتے ہیں، اسکولوں سے باہر ہیں۔ اقوام متحدہ کے ذیلی اداروں یونیسف اور یونیسکو کی جانب سے جاری کردہ تازہ ترین رپورٹ میں یہ انکشاف کیا گیا ہے کہ طالبان حکومت کی عائد کردہ پابندیوں کے باعث اب تک چھبیس لاکھ سے زائد افغان لڑکیاں ثانوی تعلیم سے مکمل طور پر محروم ہو چکی ہیں۔

طالبان رجیم کی پالیسیوں اور پابندیوں کی وجہ سے نہ صرف لڑکیوں کی تعلیم پر قدغن لگی ہے بلکہ اسکولوں میں لڑकों کے داخلوں کی شرح میں بھی نمایاں کمی دیکھنے میں آئی ہے۔ اس وقت افغانستان بھر کے اسکولوں کی مجموعی حالت انتہائی ابتر ہو چکی ہے اور وہاں بنیادی سہولیات، تربیت یافتہ اساتذہ اور معیاری تعلیمی وسائل کی شدید قلت پائی جاتی ہے۔

stories.title: اسلام آباد کے بلدیاتی انتخابات کیلئے کاغذات نامزدگی جمع کرانے کی تاریخ میں توسیع
stories.summary:
الیکشن کمیشن کی جانب سے دارالحکومت کے بلدیاتی انتخابات کے تناظر میں کاغذات نامزدگی جمع کرانے کے عمل میں دو دن کی توسیع کا فیصلہ کیا گیا ہے۔ اس حوالے سے جاری کردہ تفصیلات کے مطابق اب تمام امیدوار آٹھ نومبر دو ہزار چھبیس تک اپنے کاغذات متعلقہ ریٹرننگ افسران کے پاس جمع کرانے کے مجاز ہوں گے۔

ڈسٹرکٹ ریٹرنگ آفیسر نے اس سلسلے میں تمام امیدواروں کو خصوصی ہدایت جاری کی ہے کہ وہ مقررہ تاریخ تک اپنی تمام ضروری دستاویزات کو مکمل کرتے ہوئے کاغذات نامزدگی بروقت جمع کرائیں۔ یہ توسیع امیدواروں کو انتخابی عمل میں شرکت کے لیے تیاری اور کاغذی کارروائی مکمل کرنے کا مزید موقع فراہم کرتی ہے۔

اس فیصلے کا مقصد تمام خواہشمند افراد کو سہولت فراہم کرنا ہے تاکہ وہ بغیر کسی رکاوٹ کے اپنے انتخابی عمل کا آغاز کر سکیں۔ الیکشن کمیشن کی طرف سے مقرر کردہ اس نئی آخری تاریخ کے بعد مزید کسی قسم کی توسیع کا ذکر نہیں کیا گیا ہے۔

تمام متعلقہ امیدواروں کو تاکید کی گئی ہے کہ وہ آخری تاریخ کا انتظار کیے بغیر اپنی تمام تیاریاں مکمل کر لیں اور ریٹرننگ افسران کے دفاتر میں مقررہ وقت کے اندر اپنے کاغذات جمع کرانا یقینی بنائیں۔

stories.title: ہزارہ موٹروے پر مسافر بس اور ڈمپر میں تصادم، آٹھ افراد جاں بحق
stories.summary:
ایبٹ آباد کے قریب ہزارہ موٹروے پر حویلیاں انٹرچینج کے نزدیک ایک خوفناک ٹریفک حادثہ پیش آیا جہاں گلگت سے راولپنڈی جانے والی مسافر بس اور ایک ڈمپر آپس میں ٹکرا گئے۔ اس دردناک تصادم کے نتیجے میں آٹھ مسافر جاں بحق جبکہ متعدد افراد زخمی ہو گئے۔

ابتدائی اطلاعات کے مطابق حادثے کی وجہ بس کا ٹائر پھٹنا بنی جس کی وجہ سے ڈرائیور گاڑی پر اپنا کنٹرول برقرار نہ رکھ سکا اور بس بے قابو ہو کر سامنے موجود ڈمپر سے جا ٹکرائی۔ حادثے کی اطلاع ملتے ہی ریسکیو 1122 ایبٹ آباد کی سات ایمبولینسز اور ایک ریسکیو گاڑی فوری طور پر جائے وقوعہ پر روانہ کر دی گئی۔

ریسکیو ٹیموں نے موقع پر کارروائی کرتے ہوئے سترہ زخمیوں اور میتوں کو ابتدائی طبی امداد فراہم کرنے کے بعد ڈی ایچ کیو ہسپتال ایبٹ آباد اور ایوب میڈیکل کمپلیکس منتقل کر دیا۔ ابتدائی معلومات کے مطابق اس حادثے میں اپنی جان گنوانے والے تمام آٹھ افراد کا تعلق گلگت سے بتایا گیا ہے۔

گورنر خیبرپختونخوا فیصل کریم کنڈی نے ہزارہ موٹروے پر پیش آنے والے اس افسوسناک واقعے پر گہرے رنج و غم کا اظہار کیا ہے۔ انہوں نے متعلقہ حکام کو ہدایت کی ہے کہ ہسپتالوں میں لائے جانے والے زخمی افراد کو بہترین طبی سہولیات کی فراہمی ہر صورت یقینی بنائی جائے۔

stories.title: کراچی میں پاور ہاؤس چورنگی کے قریب اسکول وین الٹنے سے متعدد بچے زخمی
stories.summary:
کراچی کے علاقے نارتھ کراچی میں پاور ہاؤس چورنگی کے قریب ایک اسکول وین کو حادثہ پیش آگیا جس کے نتیجے میں اندر سوار متعدد بچے زخمی ہو گئے۔ ریسکیو ذرائع کے مطابق یہ حادثہ وین کے الٹنے کی وجہ سے پیش آیا جس سے گاڑی کو بھی شدید نقصان پہنچا ہے۔

واقعے کی اطلاع ملتے ہی پولیس اور ریسکیو ادارے کی ٹیمیں فوری طور پر جائے حادثہ پر پہنچ گئیں اور تمام زخمی بچوں کو طبی امداد کے لیے فوری طور پر عباسی شہید اسپتال منتقل کر دیا گیا۔ حادثے کے باعث علاقے میں اور متاثرہ بچوں کے خاندانوں میں تشویش کی لہر دوڑ گئی۔

واضح رہے کہ اس واقعے سے ایک روز قبل جمعرات کے روز بھی کراچی میں شارع فیصل پر ایک اور اسکول وین حادثے کا شکار ہوئی تھی۔ اس پچھلے واقعے میں ریوو ڈالے کی غفلت کی وجہ سے ناتھا خان پل کے قریب کئی گاڑیاں آپس میں ٹکرا گئی تھیں مگر ڈرائیور کی حاضر دماغی کی بدولت بچے معجزانہ طور پر محفوظ رہے تھے۔

اس گزشتہ واقعے میں وین کے اندر دو سال سے لے کر آٹھ سال تک کے چھوٹے بچے اور بچیاں سوار تھیں جو حادثے کے بعد شدید خوفزدہ ہو گئے تھے اور رونے لگے۔ کراچی میں لگاتار اسکول وینز کے حادثات نے والدین اور شہریوں میں حفاظتی اقدامات کے حوالے سے شدید تشویش پیدا کر دی ہے۔

stories.title: Carlos Alcaraz Advances to Paris Masters Quarter-Finals After Matteo Berrettini Withdraws
stories.summary:
Carlos Alcaraz advanced to the quarter-finals of the Paris Masters on Thursday when his scheduled opponent, Matteo Berrettini, withdrew from the tournament. Berrettini pulled out ahead of their match due to an arm injury, stating that ongoing pain prevented him from playing. Alcaraz, a seven-time Grand Slam champion who received a first-round bye as a top-eight seed, reached the last eight following a previous straight-sets victory over Alex Michelsen. 

With world number one Alexander Zverev having exited the tournament earlier in the week, Alcaraz remains the top-ranked player left in the draw. In the quarter-finals on Friday, the Spanish player is scheduled to face American Taylor Fritz. Fritz secured his place in the next round by defeating French sixth seed Arthur Fils 6-3, 6-4, keeping his hopes alive for a spot at the ATP Finals.

Berrettini, 30, has faced numerous injuries throughout his career, including a hip issue earlier this season that forced him to retire during his French Open quarter-final against Matteo Arnaldi. Meanwhile, other matches saw American third seed Ben Shelton defeat France's Arthur Rinderknech in a third-set tie-break to set up a quarter-final meeting with compatriot Tommy Paul. Paul advanced by beating Frenchman Quentin Halys.

Additional results from the tournament included Australian qualifier Rinky Hijikata defeating Tomas Martin Etcheverry following his previous win over Novak Djokovic. Lorenzo Musetti lost to France's Luca Van Assche, while former world number two Casper Ruud concluded the day's matches with a 6-3, 6-3 victory over Germany's Jan-Lennard Struff. Friday's schedule will open with Shelton playing Paul, followed by Alcaraz against Fritz and Ruud facing Nuno Borges.

stories.title: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Governor Directs Bank of Khyber to Launch Student Scooter Financing
stories.summary:
Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa Governor Faisal Karim Kundi instructed the Bank of Khyber (BoK) on Thursday to create an easy-instalment scooter financing scheme specifically for students. The directive was issued during a high-level meeting at the Governor's House in Peshawar, which was attended by Finance Adviser Tariq Mahmood Pasha, Additional Chief Secretary Planning and Development Islam Zeb, Managing Director BoK Hassan Raza, and other senior officials.

During the meeting, officials briefed the Governor on several proposed credit products targeted at youth, farmers, and entrepreneurs. These included the Ubharta Naujawan youth scheme, Agricultural Solarization, Khushhal Kisan, and industrial financing packages, alongside updates on a two-phase home solarization program covering merged districts. Governor Kundi emphasized that providing modern amenities, such as accessible student transportation, remains a key government priority.

In addition to student transport, the Governor stressed the necessity of supporting farmers through financial credit and facilitating the transition of agricultural tube-wells to solar power to counter prolonged electricity load-shedding. He also ordered bank management to fast-track upgrades to the mobile banking application to deliver faster and more reliable digital services across the province.

Governor Kundi urged officials to finalize the eligibility criteria, instalment structures, and repayment terms for the scooter scheme for the next meeting. He reiterated that the Bank of Khyber must act as a crucial tool for implementing the provincial government's socio-economic agenda by linking credit to education, agriculture, and clean energy.

stories.title: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Area Development Council Holds Inaugural Meeting in Landi Kotal
stories.summary:
The Area Development Council of Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa convened its inaugural gathering at the Landi Kotal Jirga Hall to focus on regional progress. Over 100 council members participated alongside key figures including Khyber Deputy Commissioner Shahid Ali and District Police Officer Waqar Ahmad. Former Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa governor Shaukatullah Khan presided over the session as the chairman of the council.

Attendees united behind a shared commitment to collaborate on restoring peace, advancing growth initiatives, and addressing community challenges across the 12 targeted districts. Chairman Shaukatullah Khan emphasized that the main goal of the organization is achieving lasting stability and efficiently pushing forward the development agenda within these specific areas.

Khan explained that the council incorporates delegates from diverse backgrounds to ensure local difficulties are addressed and growth goals are determined through extensive dialogue. Furthermore, he described the military as a national treasure and stated that supporters of the armed forces deserve honor. He also rejected rumors concerning the seizure of mineral deposits as unfounded rumors, advising the public to refrain from circulating misunderstandings.

The establishment of the council matters because it directly targets peace, public grievances, and infrastructure priorities across twelve designated districts through broad local representation. The initiative brings together officials, security leadership, and civilian members to coordinate future administrative and developmental steps for the region.

stories.title: Bournemouth Extends Europa League Win Streak While AC Milan Suffers Defeat
stories.summary:
Bournemouth continued their undefeated run in the UEFA Europa League on Thursday by coming from behind to secure a 3-1 victory against 10-man Sparta Prague. The Czech side initially took the lead through an individual goal by Ebrima Singhateh, after Bournemouth's Lewis Cook missed a penalty in the first half. Sparta's Tobias Guddal received a red card before half-time, allowing Bournemouth to equalize through Tyler Adams in the 57th minute. Late goals from substitutes Evanilson and Rayan secured the team's fourth consecutive European victory under manager Marco Rose.

In Italy, Ruben Amorim's AC Milan experienced a 2-0 home defeat against Ferencvaros at the San Siro. Haiti international Lenny Joseph scored twice in the second half for the visitors, who maintained a perfect record in the competition despite Bamidele Yusuf being sent off. The loss leaves Milan outside the top 24 with three points at the halfway stage of the league phase, prompting criticism from Amorim regarding his team's performance.

In other Europa League fixtures, Benfica moved to the top of the standings on goal difference after defeating Lech Poznan 3-1, with goals from Rafa Silva, Gianluca Prestianni, and Georgiy Sudakov. Bayer Leverkusen suffered their first loss of the campaign, beaten 1-0 at home by Olympique de Marseille. Crystal Palace drew 1-1 with Hoffenheim thanks to a stoppage-time equalizer from Daichi Kamada, while Celtic earned their first points by defeating Besiktas 3-2 behind two goals from substitute Camilo Duran.

In the UEFA Conference League, Brighton and Hove Albion defeated Getafe 1-0 away via a header from Malick Yalcouye. Ajax recorded a 6-1 victory over Midtjylland in Denmark, and Hearts lost 3-1 to Thun. The matches form part of the ongoing European club football calendar for November 2026.

stories.title: Karachi's New Food Walk Faces Criticism Over Seating Fees and Congestion
stories.summary:
Karachi's newly developed Sindhi Muslim food walk has drawn public criticism and controversy after visitors were reportedly asked to pay Rs600 simply to sit on chairs without purchasing food or beverages. The issue emerged after Geo Digital investigated complaints regarding restaurants demanding payment for using tables and chairs placed along the renovated pathway. A restaurant staff member claimed the fee was connected to monthly charges allegedly collected by the Karachi Metropolitan Corporation (KMC) and the relevant Town Municipal Corporation (TMC).

In response to inquiries, TMC Chanesaar Town acknowledged jurisdiction over the food walk but denied that either the town administration or the KMC was collecting fees from restaurants for utilizing the public space. The administration invited citizens to submit written complaints or photographic evidence against establishments demanding such charges so that explanations could be requested. Social media users and visitors voiced frustration, arguing that the practice discourages middle-class families from visiting the public area.

Beyond the seating fee controversy, traders have reportedly encountered difficulties following the inauguration of the project, which was modeled after streets in New York and Türkiye. Sources indicated that traders faced pressure to sign agreements for installing billboards, while restaurant sales allegedly dropped due to parking issues. The project has also sparked complaints from long-term neighborhood residents regarding increased traffic congestion.

Local resident Ghulam Hassan stated that closing the food street to vehicular traffic redirected congestion into nearby residential streets in PECHS, creating disorder and raising security concerns regarding mobile phone thefts. The complaints highlight ongoing management challenges concerning public space usage, parking arrangements, and the impact of commercial redevelopment on surrounding residential areas.

stories.title: Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz Expands Ali Dar's Official Portfolio
stories.summary:
Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz Sharif has assigned the additional portfolio of International Cooperation to her adviser Ali Dar. The appointment aims to attract foreign investment, build international partnerships, and enhance global economic engagement for the province. Following the official notification, Dar's revised title is Adviser to the Chief Minister on Artificial Intelligence, International Cooperation and Special Initiatives.

As part of this initiative, the Punjab government established the Office of International Coordination and Cooperation (OICAC), appointing Dar to lead the new body. Additionally, the Punjab Board of Investment and Trade (PBIT) has been linked with OICAC to better coordinate international investment initiatives, trade opportunities, and partnerships with foreign institutions. Dar stated that the new office will facilitate foreign investment and streamline cooperation between government departments to turn international partnerships into practical economic projects.

Ali Dar was initially appointed as Adviser to the Chief Minister on Artificial Intelligence and Special Initiatives on February 9, 2026, holding the status and powers of a provincial minister. His previous portfolio focused on promoting innovation, technology adoption, and governance improvements. Prior to joining the Punjab government, Dar founded the UAE-based HDS Group of Companies and served as its chief executive until 2024.

Dar is the eldest son of Pakistan's Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar. He is married to Asma Nawaz Sharif, the daughter of former prime minister Nawaz Sharif and sister of Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz. Educated at Aitchison College in Lahore, Dar moved to Britain in 2000, where he earned a degree in software engineering from University College London and the University of Manchester Institute of Science and Technology.

stories.title: Cristiano Ronaldo ends legendary career with 146 goals in 234 appearances
stories.summary:
Cristiano Ronaldo has officially announced his retirement from international football, concluding a stellar career spanning over two decades with the Portugal national team. Throughout his mammoth 234 appearances for the Selecao after debuting in 2003, he scored a record 146 goals, cementing his legacy as one of the sport's greatest players.

Among his standout moments, Ronaldo delivered a brilliant hat-trick in Stockholm to secure Portugal's qualification for the World Cup in Brazil at the expense of Sweden. In 2016, despite suffering an early injury and leaving the Euro 2016 final in tears against hosts France, he cheered his team on from the touchline as Eder scored an extra-time winner to secure Portugal's first major international trophy.

At the 2018 World Cup opener in Sochi, Ronaldo scored a remarkable hat-trick—including a stunning late free kick—to earn Portugal a thrilling draw against Spain. Three months after turning 40, he added another milestone by helping Portugal reach the Nations League final against Spain, scoring the winner against Germany in the semi-final and the equalizer in the decider before his side triumphed on penalties.

Later in his career during the World Cup in Toronto, Ronaldo spearheaded a crucial 2-1 victory over Croatia in the last 32. After an early goal was disallowed and Croatia took the lead, he equalized from the penalty spot before Goncalo Ramos headed in the late winner to advance Portugal.

stories.title: Carlos Alcaraz advances to Paris Masters quarter-finals after Berrettini withdraws
stories.summary:
Carlos Alcaraz advanced to the quarter-finals of the Paris Masters following the withdrawal of his scheduled round-of-16 opponent, Matteo Berrettini. The Italian player pulled out prior to their match due to ongoing elbow pain, leaving the seven-time Grand Slam champion Alcaraz through to the last eight after playing just one previous match in the tournament—a straight-sets victory over Alex Michelsen.

Alcaraz, who received a first-round bye as a top-eight seed and has never won the Paris Masters, will face American Taylor Fritz on Friday. Fritz secured his quarter-final spot by defeating French sixth seed Arthur Fils 6-3, 6-4, keeping his hopes for the ATP Finals alive. Meanwhile, Berrettini's withdrawal continues an injury-plagued season that also saw him retire early during the French Open.

In other tournament action, American third seed Ben Shelton survived a tight contest against France's Arthur Rinderknech, winning 6-3, 4-6, 7-6 in a third-set tie-break. Shelton will next face compatriot Tommy Paul, who advanced by beating Quentin Halys 7-6, 6-4. Australian qualifier Rinky Hijikata continued his strong run by defeating Tomas Martin Etcheverry 2-6, 6-3, 7-5 following his earlier upset over Novak Djokovic.

Elsewhere, Lorenzo Musetti failed to capitalize on his previous win over world number one Alexander Zverev, losing a long three-set match to Frenchman Luca Van Assche. Former world number two Casper Ruud concluded the day's matches with a 6-3, 6-3 win over Germany's Jan-Lennard Struff, setting up Friday's upcoming quarter-final clashes.

stories.title: Mourners Gather for Funeral of Deceased Footballer Jesus de Miguel
stories.summary:
Hundreds of mourners gathered in the village of Navahermosa, located roughly 100 kilometres southwest of Madrid, to attend the funeral of 30-year-old Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel. Spain's World Cup-winning coach Luis de la Fuente and Real Madrid president Florentino Perez were among the approximately 400 attendees dressed in traditional black outside the church. De Miguel passed away following a collision with Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono during a second division match. Flags flew at half-mast in Navahermosa, the birthplace of his parents where his grandparents still reside, after the local council declared three days of mourning. His Tenerife teammates served as pallbearers, carrying his coffin into the church.

During the service, De Miguel's agent read a statement on behalf of the grieving family thanking well-wishers and asking for privacy to grieve in peace. The tragedy prompted Spain's footballers' union (AFE) to request the postponement of all matches across every category for the weekend, as players expressed deep sorrow and felt normal competitive conditions were absent. Tenerife's match at Granada and Andorra's clash with Mallorca were already postponed. Tenerife plans to honor De Miguel, who played a key role in their promotion to the second tier last season, at their stadium on Saturday.

Meanwhile, Spanish police opened a judicial investigation into the incident. Owono, a 25-year-old Equatorial Guinea international, faced a torrent of racist online abuse following the collision. He released a statement expressing immense pain over the loss and stating he would face whatever issues arise with utmost respect, while focusing entirely on the tragedy. De Miguel's death marks the second time in a few months that a player has died after falling ill on the pitch, following the passing of Portuguese midfielder Quevin Castro on August 25.

stories.title: Bournemouth Extends Winning Streak with Europa League Victory Over Sparta Prague
stories.summary:
Bournemouth maintained their flawless record in the Europa League by securing a 3-1 comeback victory against 10-player Sparta Prague in the Czech Republic. Sparta initially took the lead through an individual goal from Ebrima Singhateh, which followed a missed penalty by Bournemouth's Lewis Cook that hit the post. The home side was reduced to 10 men before half-time after Tobias Guddal received a red card. Marco Rose's side capitalized in the second half when Tyler Adams equalized in the 57th minute. Substitutes Evanilson and Rayan then scored late goals to secure Bournemouth's fourth consecutive victory in the competition.

The win marks Bournemouth's seventh consecutive victory across all competitions as they prepare for a Premier League fixture against Ipswich. Manager Marco Rose emphasized the need for his team to stay sharp and maintain momentum. With this result, Bournemouth sits near the top of the standings, just behind Benfica on goal difference after the Portuguese club defeated Lech Poznan 3-1.

In other Europa League action, Ruben Amorim's AC Milan suffered a 2-0 home defeat against Ferencvaros, with Lenny Joseph scoring twice for the visitors despite Bamidele Yusuf's red card. The result leaves Milan struggling outside the top 24 with three points at the halfway stage. Elsewhere, Bayer Leverkusen lost 1-0 to Marseille, Crystal Palace drew 1-1 with Hoffenheim thanks to a stoppage-time equalizer from Daichi Kamada, and Celtic earned their first points by defeating Besiktas 3-2.

stories.title: لاہور 458 ایئر کوالٹی انڈیکس کے ساتھ دنیا کا آلودہ ترین شہر قرار
stories.summary:
